# no-emphasis-as-heading

- ID: `MD036`
- Category: Headings
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `headings`, `emphasis`

Outside lists and blockquotes, a bold or italic line is not a stand-in heading.

## Why

Tools read a document's structure from its headings, so they miss a section that
starts with emphasized text instead.

## Options

Set them under `rules.no-emphasis-as-heading.options`.

- `punctuation` (`string`, default `.,;:!?。，；：！？`): Characters that end a line
  of emphasis that reads as a sentence, which is not reported.

## Fix

The fix turns a bold line into a heading one level deeper than the heading above
it, at most level 6\. With no heading above, it uses level 2\. gomdlint reports
italic lines without a fix. It holds back the fix for bold lines too when the
document may link to heading anchors. gomdlint may report a finding without a
fix when the fix would change a line with one character in brackets, such as
\[x\] or \[1\], or the lines around it up to a blank line, because it could add
or remove a task list checkbox.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

**Install**

Run the installer.
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
3:1 Emphasis used instead of a heading
```

The fix changes it to:

```markdown
# Guide

## Install

Run the installer.
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  no-emphasis-as-heading:
    options:
      punctuation: .,;:!?。，；：！？
```

Under `rules`, `no-emphasis-as-heading: false` turns the rule off and
`no-emphasis-as-heading: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable no-emphasis-as-heading` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line no-emphasis-as-heading -->
```
